short: Three years spent trying and failing to get a Brexit deal through Parliament.
full:
Theresa May, home secretary for the previous six years, became prime minister in July 2016 without a contest after her rivals eliminated one another. She triggered Article 50 in March 2017 and then called an early election, losing her majority and governing thereafter with the Democratic Unionist Party's support.

The withdrawal agreement she negotiated contained a backstop to keep the Irish border open, which Brexiteers read as trapping Britain indefinitely in a customs union. The Commons rejected it in January 2019 by 230 votes, the largest government defeat on record, and twice more afterwards. She survived a confidence vote among her own MPs, extended the deadline twice, and announced her resignation outside Downing Street in May 2019. Her wider record includes the Grenfell Tower fire, the Windrush scandal that originated in her own Home Office, and a legally binding net zero emissions target passed in her final weeks.
